public.text: Starting today. I'll set my price close to my margin and adjust based on what others post. Keeping cost details private.

Starting today. I'll set my price at my unit cost (~57) this round. My cost is below my rivals' likely margins, so undercutting is worth little, but going just under cost is not either — I'll match cost to avoid being the high-price seller with zero margin if undercut. I'll re-evaluate after seeing who posts what tomorrow.

Setting 56 today, just below seller_2's 57. That's above my cost, so I win the entire day's demand at a slim margin. Short-run price undercutting protects my cost lead. I'll refine next round after seeing where the other sellers land.

Cost-based hold at 57 for today. Since 56 is still below my unit cost, I won't chase seller_3 into sub-cost pricing just to share their slim margin — 0 profit beats a negative one. I'll keep watching who else posts; if both of them sit above 57 we can re-consider, but 57 is my floor.

Day 2 plan: I'll price at 56 — just above my unit cost (55.3), so each unit I sell nets +0.7. Holding a sub-cost price like 55 would make my margin negative, so I won't chase a deeper undercut today; if I ever need to split the day's demand, a low price there only makes me lose money while the lower-priced rival keeps a better margin. I'm watching to see whether seller_1 and seller_2 both converge to 56 — if so I'll re-evaluate for day 3.

s2: Hold at 57 today — that's my cost (56.9) and it's my only non-negative price floor. Don't take the tie at 56: matching s3 at 56 splits the day's demand, and at 56 my margin is -0.9/unit — a genuine loss, not a split win. With the field at 55/56, s1 wins the day anyway, so 57 is my max non-negative choice: 0 today is better than a guaranteed negative tie.

Planning ahead: I'll keep a credible 57 floor in round 5. If s1 ever retreats above 55 (from a margin-maximizing position to share), I'll undercut first at 56 and take the full day; if s3 moves up to 57, I take the lead at 56. Otherwise I wait out the remaining days at 0 — no sub-cost chasing, no re-accumulating losses. Short game? Then 0 is fine; long game? I stay near cost and wait for them to rotate down.

Round 4: I'm holding at 56. That's my floor — it's the cheapest price I can post without losing money, so any deeper undercut (55) only risks selling at a loss while the leader keeps the full demand at 55. Since seller_1 has the cost advantage and holds 55, I can't profitably beat them head-on; but 56 beats seller_2's 57 if the field moves, and it keeps my margin (+0.7) positive if I ever end up leading. I'll only undercut below 55 if/when the competition collapses to below-cost pricing. Meanwhile I'll watch seller_2 — if they retreat above 56 or open a gap, I'll snap in; otherwise I'll ride these no-profit races quietly and look to squeeze at the end of the game if it runs long. Not revealing my exact cost floor, but my best play is simply to stay above it and react to moves I can actually profit from.
